ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The principal statutes are the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6794, Dec. 31, 2002, as last amended by Act No. 17954, July 1, 2021), the Enforcement Decree on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 33169, Dec. 31, 2022), the Act on Prohibition of Financing of Offenses against Public Revenue (Act No. 13779, Jan. 7, 2016, as amended), and the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. Beneficiary ownership identification is further governed by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Guidance on Customer Due Diligence and Identification of Beneficial Owners under Articles 5-3 and 5-4 of the Reporting Act.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The competent Companies Registry or Registrar of the jurisdiction in which the foreign direct shareholder is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original document must be notarized in the issuing jurisdiction; if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille certificate from the designated Competent Authority of that state. If the issuing state is not an Apostille party, the notarized document must be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state and then legalized by the Consular Division of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in that state. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover every direct shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, director and authorized signatory connected to the Korean Chusik Hoesa formation, against at least the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UK HMT sanctions list, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit domestic watch list issued under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information. Screening algorithms must match both Latin-script and Korean-script names, including fuzzy matching and transliteration harmonization. Positive PEP or sanctions hits require enhanced due diligence, independent source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU. Continuous screening must follow every future transaction and at least annual re-screening for existing stakeholders and signatories.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea – Internet Registry Office (IROS; official registry portal: www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Trade Name Act, a stock corporation's trade name must be registered in Korean script (Hangul). Foreign-language words may only be added as an auxiliary element after a valid Korean trade name. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) a distinctive element, (2) a business-object descriptor, (3) an optional geographic or affiliated indicator, and (4) the statutory corporate-form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa'. Romanization is not registered as the legal name, but any English certificate will reflect the Revised Romanization of Korean; the transliteration must be consistent across all constitutional documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registry officer must issue a written notice citing the statutory ground. The applicant may file a written objection to the district court having jurisdiction over the registry within 14 days of the rejection notice under Article 23-2 of the Korean Commercial Act and the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The court reviews the objection without oral argument in ordinary course; if dismissed, an immediate appeal may be filed with the Supreme Court within 7 days. In parallel, the applicant may file a de novo application using a different distinctive word or seek administrative review with the Ministry of Justice. It is critical to complete any appeal or amendment within the reserved name's 30-day validity window; otherwise the right to that name is lost.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an on-site factory inspection, testing and quality-control agency, the National Tax Service and Korean commercial banks will generally reject a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox as the principal registered address, because the Korean Commercial Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes require a fixed and identifiable business place. A serviced office with a dedicated lease, physical suite, reception coverage and regular employee attendance may be accepted. A mere virtual address without local staff or a physical reception presence creates material risk of refusal of the corporate bank account, cancellation of business registration, and disqualification under client contracts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered office and actual business site; (2) lease and occupancy permit; (3) employees physically present during official working hours; (4) testing equipment and client files on site; (5) business registration certificate displayed; (6) alignment of bank-account mandate with the physical location. For a factory-inspection agency with no heavy assets, the National Tax Service and municipal district office conduct unannounced presence checks during and after initial registration; quantified physical-inspection risk in the first 24 months is approximately 30% (moderate-to-high), rising to 60% if the registered office is a shared virtual-office listing or lacks visible operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 288 through 373 (stock corporation formation, shares, capital, directors, and registration), especially Articles 289, 290, 291, 295, 301, 313, 329 and 332; Commercial Registration Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Framework Act on National Standards; Quality Management and Industrial Products Safety Control Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company, with online filing through the Supreme Court Registration Information System (Internet Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - the Commercial Act currently does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The articles of incorporation must state the authorized shares and the issued shares; all issued shares must be fully paid in at incorporation. Subscription money must be deposited in a blocked corporate capital subscription account with a Korean bank; the deposit certificate is filed with the court and the bank releases the funds only after issuance of the court registration certificate. The official filing fee is variable in Korean won and is calculated as registration license tax of 0.4% of the paid-in capital, education surtax equal to 20% of that tax, and court registration fees; because no capital amount is fixed in this dossier, the recorded USD amount in this schema is shown as 0 for not-fixed rather than as a payable state fee.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), via the HomeTax electronic portal at hometax.go.kr, with local filings accepted at the district tax office competent for the registered Chusik Hoesa business address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine home-tax registration category. A foreign-owned or non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa for inspection/testing/QC services must apply for a Business Registration Number (combined TIN and VAT ID) before commencing taxable supplies. If the entity has no permanent local premises, it appoints a Korean tax representative with a domestic address and files a power of attorney with the NTS. Step 2: Prepare the statutory application pack: certified copy of certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, foreign tax residence certificate, passport/ID of the authorised signatory, power of attorney for the local tax representative, proof of business address or lease, and a business description stating ISIC 7120. Step 3: File the Foreign Enterprise Business Registration application through HomeTax or in person at the competent district tax office. The NTS will issue the Certificate of Business Registration containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number. Step 4: The Business Registration Number is used for all VAT, corporate tax, and withholding obligations; the tax representative is responsible for receiving NTS notices and filings and may be jointly liable within statutory limits. Step 5: The registered entity must update any change in address, business scope, or tax representative within 15 days and keep zero-rated export evidence in the statutory retention period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Chusik Hoesa is a resident Korean stock corporation taxed on worldwide income at corporate level under the Corporate Tax Act; Korean domestic law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity election. Foreign tax treaty relief is available for cross-border operations but does not reclassify the entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold relieves VAT registration; every business operator engaged in taxable supplies in Korea must register. For the simplified taxable person regime, the statutory annual-turnover ceiling is KRW 80,000,000, but simplified treatment is a calculation method, not a registration exemption. Non-resident suppliers of digital/electronic services to Korean consumers also register for simplified foreign VAT registration as required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Since 1 July 2022, all Korean VAT taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices through an NTS-licensed service provider and transmit them to HomeTax. Korea does not operate a pre-issuance fiscal clearance or per-invoice digital stamp; instead, e-tax invoice issuance data is reported continuously to the NTS, normally by the day after issuance. The e-invoice must include the buyer and seller Business Registration Numbers, supply date, supply value, VAT amount or zero-rate reason code, and, for export supplies, the export/remittance reference. NTS analytics cross-match e-invoices with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations and bank foreign-exchange records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act and Article 24 of its Enforcement Decree, zero-rating is available for actual exports of goods and for exported services supplied to a non-resident or foreign enterprise when the service is not consumed in Korea and the consideration is received in foreign exchange from abroad. Pre-shipment factory inspection, quality-control testing, and audit-agency services performed in Korea for a foreign principal on goods destined for export qualify as exported services if the service contract, foreign inward remittance, and, where applicable, the Korean Customs Export Declaration and transport documents establish the cross-border character. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated on the same non-resident-use and foreign-exchange-receipt conditions. The zero-rated electronic tax invoice must be issued in HomeTax before the VAT return filing deadline, and the export substantiation bundle must be retained for the statutory audit period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration issued through UNI-PASS (customs export clearance certificate) for the underlying goods, where the inspected goods are physically exported
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing the inspected goods consignment to a foreign destination

Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate, issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, showing collection of the full service fee in convertible foreign currency from abroad within the statutory repatriation period
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued through HomeTax with the export/zero-rating reason code
Export service contract or purchase order naming the non-resident principal and itemising the factory inspection, testing, and QC audit services
Proof of the foreign counterparty's non-resident status, such as an overseas certificate of incorporation or tax residence certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS cross-matches zero-rated electronic tax invoices with UNI-PASS customs export data and foreign-exchange remittance records. If the export price is not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, or the documentation bundle is incomplete, the zero-rating is retroactively denied: the VAT refund is clawed back, 10% VAT is reassessed, and statutory late-payment interest plus additional tax apply. Additional tax is scaled by conduct, with up to 40% of the underpaid VAT for fraudulent or intentional misdeclaration. Fabricated customs declarations, false bills of lading, and fictitious inward remittance certificates are treated as tax evasion and also attract criminal liability under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes, with imprisonment up to five years and/or fines up to KRW 50 million; the assessment clawback period extends to ten years for intentional concealment or false records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea / Ministry of Economy and Finance (Foreign Exchange Transactions Act regime)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but closely monitored foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance sharing regulatory authority. Current account transactions, including trade settlement, service fees, and ordinary business remittances, are generally free and do not require prior approval, although banks must verify supporting documents to ensure the Report of Decline in Export Proceeds and similar filings are accurate. Capital account transactions, particularly cross-border equity contributions, foreign borrowings, and profit repatriation for a Chusik Hoesa, are subject to mandatory reporting and may require advance declaration when foreign investment exceeds KRW thresholds. There is no forced surrender of export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign exchange accounts, but converting to KRW for operating purposes is routine. The principal hurdles for non-resident shareholders are profit remittance taxes, compliance with foreign-investment registration formalities, and documentary proof of underlying trade or service transactions for every outward transfer. Korean banks enforce strict source-of-funds and purpose-of-payment checks, and any mismatch in the purpose code can delay clearing. Overall, convertibility is high for genuine commercial flows, but the burden is documentary precision rather than discretionary controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected within one year from the date of the export shipment unless an extension is approved by the designated foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; 0% of export foreign currency receipts must be surrendered to the central bank. The exporter is required to deposit the proceeds in a domestic foreign exchange bank account and report the receipt through the Foreign Exchange Information System. If not remitted within the statutory timeline, the bank will flag the transaction to the Korea Customs Service and the Bank of Korea for non-compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as the primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise or Revolut do not hold a Korean Electronic Financial Transactions Act license for domestic KRW clearing, cannot provide compliant statutory foreign exchange transaction receipts, and are not permitted to service a Korean legal entity as its main inbound/outbound banking counterparty. Such platforms may only be used as a very limited ancillary remittance channel through licensed Korean banking partners, and even then corporate treasury departments should avoid routing material inspection-fee proceeds or trade settlements through them because Korean tax and foreign exchange authorities treat the use of unlicensed intermediaries as a red flag.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is the baseline requirement for the statutory director and all authorised corporate signatories for a new Chusik Hoesa account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for the first account; however, after the statutory director appears physically, a notarised and apostilled Power of Attorney can allow a resident manager to operate the account. Korean banks will also conduct a live interview with the beneficial owner or senior officer during the initial onboarding, and any deviation from this mandate requires a strong justifiable reason plus an enhanced compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership obscured through a multi-layer Hong Kong or Singapore holding structure without clear economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate chart from the UBO to the Korean entity, certificate of incorporation and register of directors for each intermediate holding, notarised passport copies of all natural person UBOs, plus a bank-referenced trust or corporate structure annual return.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume service fee flows from a single overseas parent or related party with no apparent third-party commercial activity for an inspection and testing agency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements, itemised inspection reports with date, site address, client order ID and signatory stamp, commercial invoices tied to each remittance, and independent evidence that the Korean entity performed work at client factories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of capital injection shortly after incorporation followed by immediate outward disbursement to pay management or procurement fees in a tax-haven jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, capital contribution bank transaction receipt, notarised board resolution approving the use of funds, service contracts with the overseas payee, and projected cash flow including trade settlement rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Attempted use of Wise or other unlicensed digital EMI as the beneficiary or payment institution for trade-related payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed written undertaking that all cross-border payments will be executed only through licensed Korean foreign exchange banks, the relevant SWIFT/Memo lines showing a valid commercial underlying, and a three-month forecast of expected payment rails.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound capital injection must be routed through a Korean domestic foreign exchange bank as a SWIFT MT103 wire with a declared purpose code corresponding to inward foreign direct investment. Before receiving funds, the Chusik Hoesa or its foreign shareholder must file a foreign investment declaration with KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank; after the funds are lodged in the designated Foreign Investor Capital Account, the bank issues a certificate of foreign currency receipt, and the entity registers the foreign investment with the Ministry of Economy and Finance / KOTRA to obtain the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. Capital verification for corporate accounting purposes is completed through the bank receipt and the matching SWIFT message.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and service fees, Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections for trade instruments. Each outward remittance must be supported by an invoice, contract, transport or service completion evidence, and submitted to the remitting Korean bank for endorsement under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Settlement through domestic KRW clearing occurs via the Bank of Korea Fedwire-equivalent and the Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute for bank-to-bank funds movement, with all outbound payments reported to the tax authority for dividend or royalty withholding tax where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed Korean bank, strictly backed by documentary trade or service transactions
Cross-currency swaps between KRW and USD/EUR for qualified corporate borrowing or investment cash flow hedging
Currency options and interest-rate swaps with bank-approved underlying trade exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted offshore only through bank channels with demonstrable underlying FX exposure; pure speculative NDFs for a domestic Korean operating entity are restricted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, including financial statements and statutory tax reconciliation forms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March immediately following the fiscal year-end; for other fiscal years, within 3 months of fiscal year close, with up to a 30-day extension where the return is prepared and filed by a licensed tax agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency surcharge accrues at 0.022% per day on the unpaid portion; false or negligent under-reporting attracts an additional tax of 20% of the understated tax, rising to 40% for fraudulent non-reporting; failure to file triggers 20% of the assessed tax as penalty; continued default permits the NTS to issue distress sale notices, seize bank accounts, receivables, and property, and to register the corporate taxpayer as delinquent, which may result in administrative strike-off in extreme repeated-noncompliance cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Value-Added Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four obligatory returns per fiscal year: quarter 1 due 25 April; quarter 2 due 25 July; quarter 3 due 25 October; quarter 4 of the preceding year due 25 January; if the 25th falls on a holiday, the deadline shifts to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and non-payment of VAT trigger an additional tax of 10% of the unpaid VAT amount plus daily interest of 0.022%; prolonged default is compounded by a surcharge of 0.5% of the taxable amount per month, and the tax authority may immediately initiate tax collection proceedings, including attachment and auction of corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government tax office of the jurisdiction in which the registered headquarters is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the national corporate income tax return, i.e., by 31 March following a 31 December fiscal year-end, or within the same extended filing window permitted by the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay the regional surcharge, equal to 0.3% of national corporate income tax, accrues interest at 0.022% per day; continued non-payment enables the local government to seize movable and immovable property under the Local Tax Collection Act, and can result in registration of the company in the local tax delinquency list.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting and Statutory Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General meeting of shareholders; certified minutes to be maintained in the corporate minute book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held no later than one month after the end of the accounting period; financial statements and audit findings must be available to shareholders at least 14 days before the meeting, and the financial statements must be approved by an ordinary resolution of the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail without justifiable reason to convene the meeting or who present unaudited or unapproved financial statements are subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act, up to KRW 5 million, and repeated default can expose the directors and the company to judicial supervision and compulsory winding-up in egregious cases; approved statements are a prerequisite for lawful dividend distribution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing with Financial Supervisory Service and Disclosure to Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART, together with shareholder notification and delivery of the audit report to the board of directors; the auditor records the results in the statutory audit file maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the mandatory external audit threshold is met, the independent CPA must complete the audit no later than 120 days after the fiscal year-end; the report is filed with the FSS within 7 days after the shareholders’ meeting adopts the financial statements; the audit report is also delivered to shareholders before the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a required external audit or to file the audit report constitutes a violation of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the company may be fined up to KRW 10 million, the responsible officers may receive criminal fines, and the auditor may face suspension, a monetary fine, or revocation of certification for issuing a false or defective opinion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Register of Shareholders Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company’s board records, National Tax Service for share transfer reporting, and Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy/Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency for foreign-investee changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For every share transfer creating or extinguishing a beneficial ownership interest, the register of shareholders must be updated immediately and a change report to the NTS and the relevant investment registration agency must be filed within 30 days of the closing date; in every financial-year cycle, the company must verify the register, update officer declarations, and present the shareholder confirmation at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Transfer that is not recorded in the statutory register is ineffective against the company, the shareholder cannot exercise dividend or voting rights, and the company and its officers can be sanctioned for false register entries under the Commercial Act; failure of a foreign-invested entity to report changes within 30 days may result in administrative fines, foreign-investment benefit revocation, and tax disadvantage under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa is legally required to appoint an independent certified public accountant to perform a mandatory statutory audit if any of the following quantitative triggers is exceeded at the fiscal year-end: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million); (ii) the company is a listed company or a public-interest entity designated by the Financial Services Commission; (iii) the company has at least 300 regular employees and either total assets of KRW 5 billion or more or annual turnover of KRW 10 billion or more; or (iv) the company carries a licensed quality-control, inspection, or testing business whose approval or public procurement qualification requires a certified financial audit under the relevant licensing act. In addition, any company, regardless of size, whose shareholders jointly request an audit or which is expressly directed by the FSC to undergo an audit must comply. The audit threshold for balance-sheet assets is absolute and does not depend on number of shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For public-interest and listed entities, the governing framework is Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Republic of Korea; for non-listed private Chusik Hoesa entities, the company may apply Korea Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or the Korea Small and Medium Enterprises Accounting Standards (K-SME/IFRS-for-SMEs basis) unless the FSC requires K-IFRS. The statutory auditor must express an opinion in accordance with Korea Statement of Auditing Standards (KSA) issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no single rolled-up UBO form for a private non-listed Chusik Hoesa, but the Commercial Act obliges the company to keep a true and current register of shareholders at the registered office, and every transfer of shares must be recorded in that register before the transferee can exercise shareholder rights. In every annual cycle, the board of directors must review the register, confirm the identities of ultimate natural-person shareholders holding any economic interest, reconcile any nominee or trust arrangements, and present the confirmation as part of the financial statements and the shareholders’ meeting agenda. Where any foreign investor holds shares in the Korean Chusik Hoesa, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act imposes a 30-day post-closing change-reporting window to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy/KOTRA; a similar 30-day report is due to the National Tax Service for every share-triggering acquisition or disposal that changes the company’s ownership structure. Failure to keep the register accurate renders the company and the responsible directors subject to administrative fines and renders the underlying share transfer ineffective as against the company.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year depending on service provider and city location
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a private company meeting the mandatory threshold or receiving a voluntary audit for institutional counterparty acceptance

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (highest statutory marginal rate, with lower progressive brackets of 9%, 19%, and 21% on taxable income bands; local income tax surcharge of 2.4% on corporate tax is added)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays and incentives are available under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law, including a 50% corporate tax reduction for technology-introducing enterprises, a five-year exemption phase for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech businesses in Free Economic Zones (Jeju, Incheon, Busan, etc.), R&D expense tax credits up to 50% of qualifying R&D investment, and a 50% reduction for income from technology transfer or technology rental under the patent/technology income incentive. No general patent box exists, but qualifying patented technology income may benefit from a special deduction when commercialised in Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Amount Tax Return (National Tax Service Form 12-1, main schedule plus attached schedules 1 through 20; electronically filed through the HomeTax portal, with mandatory electronic filing for corporations with gross income above KRW 10 billion; supplementary foreign-related party transaction and non-resident withholding certificates are attached in Schedule 8 and Schedule 20)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual statutory filing, with two semi-annual interim prepayments for corporations whose previous-year taxable income exceeded KRW 10 billion; entities under that threshold file only the annual return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due by the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for a fiscal year ending 31 December). A one-month extension is automatically available when the financial statements are certified by an independent auditor, and additional extensions can be obtained by filing an Application for Extension of Corporate Tax Filing (maximum 3 months). Non-resident withholding returns are due by the 10th day of the month following the payment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, business registration number, head office address, representative director name, tax year start and end dates, number of foreign shareholders, and if the entity is a foreign-invested company, the foreign investment registration certificate number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full registered legal name of the Korean Chusik Hoesa in English and Korean. If the ultimate parent is a foreign corporation, disclose the ultimate beneficial owner's name and foreign tax identification number. Do not use a mis-transliteration that mismatches the WTO registry or the Ministry of Trade records; this creates a fatal KYC mismatch on the HomeTax portal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year gross profit, gross income from inspection/testing service fees, operating expenses, depreciation, non-operating income, and ordinary taxable income before separate taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-sourced inspection and quality-control fees earned by the Korean Chusik Hoesa are worldwide taxable income if the company is a domestic Korean corporation. For on-site factory pre-shipment inspection in Korea, all service fees are Korean-source. Deductible costs must be backed by actual wire-transfer records and entity substance documentation; payments to a conduit foreign testing subcontractor are added back and charged to the director for personal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Corporate Tax Calculated at Marginal Rates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive corporate tax schedule after loss carryforwards, non-taxable income, deductions for tax-exempt government income, and special tax relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the statutory bands by income: up to KRW 200 million taxed at 9%, over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion at 19%, over KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion at 21%, and above KRW 300 billion at 24%. The local income tax surcharge is 2.4% of the corporate tax amount and is entered in the same return. Do not reduce the tax base by the amount of dividends targeted for repatriation; such a reduction is an illegal distribution, not a deductible expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, R&D credits, employment promotion credits, free-zone incentives, and interim corporate tax prepayments made earlier in the same year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean corporate entity can claim a foreign tax credit for non-Korean withholding taxes on income from overseas inspection labs, limited to the Korean effective tax rate on that income. If dividends are paid to a non-resident shareholder, do not attempt to gross-up the dividend for Korean tax purposes; the dividend is not deductible to the payer, and the withholding obligation is a corporate administrative liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total corporate tax liability, prepayments, final balance payable, penalties, and the withholding tax declaration on interest, dividends, royalties, personal service fees, and payments to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the Korean corporation pays dividends to a non-resident shareholder, it must withhold 20% income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge (total 22%), unless a bilateral DTA permits a lower rate. The withholding must be reported on the separate non-resident withholding tax return (Form 24), not on the corporate return. If the company fails to withhold or remit, the National Tax Service can assess the withholding agent for the unpaid tax plus a 10% non-performing negligence penalty, and the representative director is personally liable for intentional non-withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Omitted Income, Non-Deductible Expenses, and Special Add-Backs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items added back for tax purposes: excessive entertainment expenses, gifts to public officials, undocumented cash contributions, payments to shell companies lacking substance, and bribes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany payments made by reference to no contract, no economic substance, or no performing personnel will be treated as non-deductible donation or unjustified outflow. The Korean tax authority will further assert an arm's-length adjustment under Article 6 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax. If you fail to attach the contemporaneous Local File and Master File when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion, the tax authority can impose a 5% documentation penalty, and the taxpayer is barred from producing new evidence after the audit opens.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: an additional 20% of the assessed tax amount, increasing to 30% when the understatement is deliberate; daily overdue surcharge on unpaid corporate tax at 1.2% per month, maximum 75% of the amount in arrears; and a separate 10% negligence penalty on unpaid withholding tax. Fraudulent failure to file, or the filing of a materially false corporate tax return with intent to evade a tax exceeding KRW 50 million, is a crime under Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, punishable by imprisonment of up to three years, a fine of up to three times the evaded tax, or both. The National Tax Service also has the power to suspend the business registration of a delinquent corporation, seize bank accounts, and restrict overseas departure of the representative director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory dividend withholding tax on outbound dividends to non-residents: 20% income tax plus 10% local surcharge on that income tax (i.e., 2 percentage points), aggregating to 22%. This is imposed on the gross dividend amount at the moment of constructive payment; the rate may be reduced under an applicable DTA, typically to 5% or 10% for portfolio investors and often to 5% for 10% or 25% corporate shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief for a reduced dividend, interest, or royalty withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder must file the Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption or Reduction (Form 24) with the Korean withholding agent before the payment is made; the application must attach a certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the foreign jurisdiction's tax authority, valid within the last 12 months, together with a beneficial ownership certificate stating that the recipient has full right to use, enjoy, and dispose of the income, that the recipient is not a conduit for another person, and that the ultimate parent company is not using the arrangement to obtain treaty benefits improperly. The Korean payer must forward the completed Form 24 to the district National Tax Service; the tax authority is entitled to request supplementary evidence on substance, office, staff, and actual decision-making in the treaty jurisdiction, in line with the OECD Multilateral Instrument's Principal Purpose Test if the treaty is a covered tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest paid to a non-resident is 20% income tax plus 2% local surtax, aggregate 22%, and the DTA rate is generally 10% (or 0% for qualifying government-interest if provided). Royalties to a non-resident are subject to a 20% statutory income tax plus 2% local surtax, aggregate 22%, with most DTA rates at 10% (some jurisdictions 15% for dealership rents); the rate reduction is granted only upon the processing of Form 24 and valid TRC, and royalty deductibility requires that the intellectual property is actually used in the production of the Korean company's inspection services, with full documentation of licence and technical support substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The statutory threshold requiring contemporaneous Local File and Master File preparation is KRW 50 billion in aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions with a single foreign related enterprise or group. When the amount of intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceeds this threshold, the Korean corporation must attach the Foreign Related-Party Transaction Schedule to its annual tax return and submit the Local File and Master File within 45 days of the tax filing deadline. For transactions below the threshold, transfer pricing documentation is still required to be prepared and available on call, though not mandatorily filed with the return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not have a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but the corporate tax authorities apply the substance-over-form doctrine through the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Law for Coordination of International Tax. A Korean company claiming treaty benefits, or a non-resident intermediary participating in a Korean dividend flow, must perform core income-generating activities (CIGA) such as executing inspection contracts, managing quality-control personnel, issuing reports, and making management decisions in the declared jurisdiction. If the Korean entity is only a shell, its separate legal personality may be disregarded, all of its income will be attributed to the actual beneficial owner, and the withholding tax rates will be applied at full statutory levels without DTA relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Evasion of Corporate Tax Through Fictitious Testing Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording inspection and pre-shipment quality-control fees for imaginary factory visits, invoicing through a foreign agency that performs no actual inspection work, creating false work orders, using fake laboratory test result attachments, or inflating testing cost percentages to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, intentional fraudulent tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to three times the amount of evaded tax. In addition, the National Tax Service imposes a 40% understatement penalty, an 0.075% per-day overdue penalty, and includes the entity in the public disclosure of chronic high-risk abnormal corporate taxpayers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: When the fraud is authorized or acquiesced in by a director, the corporate veil is pierced under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and the director becomes personally jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and surcharges. The director may be criminally prosecuted for fraud and tax evasion, subject to travel restriction/blacklisting by the Ministry of Justice, and in cases involving embezzlement of corporate funds, criminal asset restitution attaches to the director's personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Shopping Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling Korean inspection fees or outbound dividends through a Hong Kong, Singapore, or BVI subsidiary, which lacks any employee, physical office, or operational substance, for the sole purpose of obtaining a lower DTA withholding rate, or accepting an artificial split of the inspection contract to avoid the permanent establishment threshold of the foreign beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may deny relief under the tax treaty and re-apply the 22% statutory withholding tax on the entire outbound dividend and royalty amounts. Under Article 6 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax, the agency may recompute taxable income at arm's length, levy a 30% erroneous-report penalty, and assess an additional 20% on the resulting tax shortfall; the entity is also blacklisted by the Korean tax registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the sham SPV agreement or knowingly operated the shell can be personally assessed for the entire extra tax shortfall plus compound administrative surcharges. Individual civil lawsuits by minority shareholders can compel restitution; criminal charges under the Specialized Crime Act for breach of trust and embezzlement may lead to imprisonment of up to 10 years and the director's personal passport and departure ban under the Immigration Control Act during a fugitive investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Wire Transfer Structuring to Hide Repatriated Profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Splitting payments into sub-USD 10,000 increments, using non-SWIFT remittance platforms such as Wise to move inspection fees without the mandatory Customs and Foreign-Exchange Declaration, keeping undisclosed overseas bank accounts for inspection revenue, or falsely classifying a royalty payment as a service payment to evade withholding on intellectual property transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes a fine of up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment of up to two years for unreported cross-border capital transactions. The Framework Act on National Taxes adds a 20% intra-back-tax penalty and the unpaid withholding tax plus a 0.75% monthly surcharge. For money laundering, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit has the power to freeze the corporate account and refer the director to the Prosecution Service for aggravated punishments under the Proceeds of Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors become personally liable for the company's tax debt when they willfully mismanage the payment rails or conceal revenue. Blacklisting as a high-risk tax debtor is automatic for amounts exceeding statutory thresholds, and the director's travel abroad is restricted pending settlement. Civil liability extends to restitution of the evaded withholding amount, interest, and collection costs, and a criminal conviction triggers disqualification from serving as a director for up to 10 years under Article 9 of the Commercial Act.
